title: I can't code a deckbuilder. Claude Code and my own asset packs did it anyway: 10 heroes, 99 enemies, 156 cards
author: _AssetSmithy_
selftext:
I make and sell 2D game assets on itch (backgrounds, battlers, card frames, icons, UI). This time I wanted to build a full game out of them, so I did.  
  
This is Clanbound, a roguelike deckbuilder in the vein of Monster Train and Wildfrost. You summon creatures onto a battle line, play spells and attacks, and fight your way through 3 acts to the final boss.  
  
What's in it:  
\- 10 heroes, each with their own deck and starting relic  
\- 156 cards (67 of them creatures) across 7 clans  
\- 99 enemies, including 27 elites and 11 bosses  
\- 44 relics, 12 potions, card upgrades  
\- 28 events with voiced NPCs who react to your choices, 132 spoken lines  
\- A branching map of 15 floors per act, with merchant, campfire, treasure, save and continue  
  
How I made it:  
The art and music come from my own asset packs, created with AI tools and cleaned up by me. The NPC voices and sound effects were generated separately with ElevenLabs. Every line of code was written by Claude Code. I set the direction, played every build and gave feedback, from "the shadow is in the wrong place" to "make the campfire look more real". Even the effects like the fire, the heat shimmer and the depth of field in the backgrounds are shaders Claude wrote.  
  
The version you can play is a second build. The first one was Unity WebGL and took close to a minute to load, which kills a browser game. So Claude ported the whole thing to plain HTML5 and PixiJS, no engine, 1:1 including the shaders and the particle effects. We ran both builds side by side on the same seeds and the combat came out identical. Now it is playable a few seconds after you open the page.  
  
It's free and runs right in your browser. Balancing is still done by feel, so any feedback is welcome: what's too easy, too hard, what's missing?  
  
**You can play it here:** [https://assetsmithy.itch.io/clanbound](https://assetsmithy.itch.io/clanbound)

comments.author: Ziadjbt78
comments.body: Love the gameplay and animation, truly impressive. How long it took you to code with Claude? I’m sure despite AI involvement this takes quite a long time and loads of effort to put together am I right? Whats your plans for the future? Expansions, improvements, etc?

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
Thanks, that means a lot!  
  
The browser version took about six hours of hands-on time over two evenings. The build in the video took longer, and on top of that come the asset packs themselves, which took months.   
  
So yes, you are right. The AI writes the code fast, but it does not know what is fun, what is unreadable on screen or what feels off in the third fight. That part is still me, and that is where the time goes. I play, note things like "the map wastes half the parchment", and it gets fixed in minutes instead of hours. The speed is real, the direction is not free.  
  
Plans: balancing first, since it is still done by feel, then more events and cards. It stays free, it is a showcase for my asset packs, so no paid expansions. Tell me what felt too easy or too hard and that is what the next pass is built on.

comments.author: Alarmed2814
comments.body: I'm not an ai hater at all, but this is just a straight up copy and reskin of slay the spire.

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
Fair, and I am not going to argue the frame: map nodes, acts, relics, potions, campfire, shop, energy, block, vulnerable, intents - that is the Slay the Spire template and I built on it on purpose.  
  
What is actually different is the unit layer. 67 of the 156 cards are creatures you summon onto a battle line. They attack on their own at the end of your turn, and enemy attacks hit your front unit instead of you. There is not a single card in the game that gives the hero block - all block goes on your units. So the defensive game is "who do I put in front and keep alive", not "do I play Defend this turn".  
  
Art is all from my own asset packs, nothing is reskinned. It is free, so if you play it and it still feels like the same game to you, I would honestly like to hear at which point.

replies.author: loulibra

WHY DOES EVERY DEV USE AI TO REPLY TO MESSAGES.

It's fucking insane, don't people realize they sound like insane robots when they reply like this???

replies.author: Jessica___
replies.body: It is pretty funny that since these AI models got popular, a chunk of people on the internet all started talking the same way.

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
There are several reasons why it sounds like a "robot".  
  
First: If you work in an office or are even a civil servant, you write emails like that, probably 100 a day, that sound just like this. That's called formal!  
  
Second: Why should I take the time and effort to formulate several sentences, when AI can do it in just a few seconds?  
  
That's the difference.  
  
Nevertheless, I'm used to phrases like that, so don't take it personally.

replies.author: ibDABIN
replies.body: Why should you? Because it shows consideration and care when you don't delegate your interactions with other people.

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
That's an interesting premise, but it's questionable whether consideration is really shown by who came up with the exact wording, or by the actual content of what's being said. If I use AI to phrase my own thoughts more clearly or politely, the decision about what gets said is still mine. That's no different from someone using a spell-checker, a translator, or, back in the day, a secretary to type up a letter. Nobody back then would've said that dictating a letter to a secretary showed less respect for the recipient.  
  
Consideration is shown by whether I actually take the time for the content and the real intent behind it, not by whether I personally typed every single word.

replies.author: ibDABIN
replies.body:
It's not questionable unless you want to rub against the grain of society. You are demonstrating you don't care enough to spend the trivial amount of time it takes to share your own thoughts and feelings without the embellishment and articulation of an AI lens. You are hiding yourself behind a delegation of processors. It's very different from a spell checker or a translator lol. I can tell I'm talking to Claude right now and that makes this whole exchange feel hollow and meaningless but I'm participating anyways to impress upon you the importance of human interaction...however little of it may be actually happening right now. And you're totally wrong in your secretary example. That's EXACTLY the sort of thing that makes a person feel dismissed.

The problem is the content is not yours. You are feeding bullet points of your thoughts and feelings into a machine for elaboration. People are asking for your thoughts and feelings. If you don't have the time to articulate them yourself, you have started the conversation already disconnected and what even is the point then?

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
I read every comment and reply to each one. Accusing me of not putting in the time is simply out of touch, just like claiming I'm feeding the AI bullet points.  
  
But I think we should probably end the discussion here, since from my point of view it's not leading anywhere anymore. There will always be people who do nothing but complain and speak negatively about anything new or changing - the eternal naysayers, in other words - and there are people who accept it, recognize the advantages, and use them to their benefit.   
  
In my eyes, you probably don't belong to the latter.  
  
But now it would be nice if you could finally comment on my actual game ;)

replies.body: You right. Each hero currently draws from about 55 cards, which is less than StS. Warrior and Dwarf even share the same pool, that one is on me. I am filling out the clans and giving each hero more cards of their own.

replies.author: Blaike325
replies.body: How many cards are unique to a specific character? If you’re saying that one character (of which if I’m reading your post right you say there are 10), has a card pool of 55, the overlap for each character has to be absolutely massive, I’m guessing 5-15 unique cards per character at most?

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
You are guessing too high. Right now it is one exclusive card per hero, except the Death Knight who has 18 because a whole clan is his alone. The rest is differentiated by clan combination, and that is not enough.  
  
I am giving each hero their own set of cards and filling out the clans. Thanks for pushing on this, most useful comment so far.

replies.author: Blaike325
replies.body: How many clans are there? And have you played slay the spire? If not I would heavily recommend playing it and also some mods people have made for new characters. Each character tends to have three archetypes and those archetypes tend to overlap in terms of build ins Ike ways so that each run feels somewhat unique

replies.author: _AssetSmithy_
replies.body:
Seven clans, each hero gets two plus the neutral cards.  
  
On archetypes: the clans have themes (poison, block, summoning, burn, healing, thorns, strength) but not three overlapping paths per hero.  
  
Just added: 224 cards instead of 156, 70 per hero instead of 55, four hero-only cards each instead of one.  
  
Update coming soon...
